Operate the work flows (the puzzle of actions and results).

```text
A FLOW is work driven by shape rather than by memory.

An ACTION (flows/actions/*.action.md) declares what it does and which RESULTS it
offers. A FLOW (flows/*.flow.md) fits actions together and says where each result
goes. What used to be a rule to remember ("NEVER close with a blocking gate red")
becomes the absence of a fitting: the BARRED result has no link to `done`.
```

## Uso

```bash
anchors flow
```

## Subcomandos

### `anchors flow build`

Scan flows/ and write the flow graph into the map.

#### Uso

```bash
anchors flow build [flags]
```

#### Flags

| Flag | Padrão | O que faz |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--root` | `.` | project root |

### `anchors flow next`

The VALID exits of a step — the command that drives.

```text
Answers "from here, where can I go", instead of listing everything and
asking someone to choose. It is what separates having a flow from having one more
document.
```

#### Uso

```bash
anchors flow next <step> [flags]
```

#### Flags

| Flag | Padrão | O que faz |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--root` | `.` | project root |

### `anchors flow show`

Draw the flow — assembled at RUNTIME from the graph.

```text
Draws the flow from the graph, never from a stored diagram.

A versioned diagram ages against the flow it describes, and the repository already
measured what that costs (see the docs-fresh gate). Here the drawing is derived,
so it cannot diverge.
```

#### Uso

```bash
anchors flow show [flow] [flags]
```

#### Flags

| Flag | Padrão | O que faz |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--direction` | `TD` | diagram direction: TD (top-down, tree-like) or LR (left to right) |
| `--mermaid` |  | emit the diagram as mermaid (boxes and arrows, for rendering) |
| `--root` | `.` | project root |

## A fila de trabalho — família

Comandos da mesma família — o que distingue cada um:

| Comando | O que faz |
| --- | --- |
| [`anchors next`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/next/) | Pull and claim the next item from the queue (the worker calls this) |
| [`anchors queue`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/queue/) | List live tasks (the work the watcher queued) |
| [`anchors work`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/work/) | Emit the work prompt of a stage (spec\|code\|feature\|test\|review) for a target |
| [`anchors done`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/done/) | Close claimed task(s) (moves to the .anchors/done/ history) |
| [`anchors drop`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/drop/) | Discard a task from the queue without completing it (removes; does not archive) |
| [`anchors reclaim`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/reclaim/) | Return to the queue the tasks stuck in claimed (dead worker) |
| [`anchors deliver`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/deliver/) | Record the delivery of a stage — the review trigger |
| [`anchors decided`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/decided/) | Release the card `escalate --for-user` stopped, once the decision is made |
| [`anchors discard`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/discard/) | Take off the board the card that no longer makes sense, without deleting it |
| [`anchors unblock`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/unblock/) | Open the work card that unblocks a card stuck in `needs-user` |
| [`anchors escalate`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/escalate/) | Open the issue for a change needed in the plan or the spec |
| [`anchors report-bug`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/report-bug/) | Report a bug in Anchors itself at github.com/co2-lab/anchors |
| [`anchors synthesize`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/synthesize/) | Two PRs conflicting in CONTENT become a synthesis card |
| [`anchors watch`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/watch/) | The background watcher: sees changes and QUEUES work |
| **`anchors flow`** | Operate the work flows (the puzzle of actions and results) |
| [`anchors board`](/pt/docs/cli/commands/board/) | The project board — published by the pipeline, or served live |

<!-- cli-reference:end -->

O Anchors permite desenvolvimento assistido por IA contínuo e ordenado através de uma fila reativa de tarefas.

---

## 1. O Ciclo do Watcher e da Fila

1. **`anchors watch`**: Roda em background. Quando um arquivo é salvo (ex: `order.spec.md`), o watcher percebe o que falta e enfileira a próxima ação (`criar-feature`, `implementar-codigo`, `rodar-testes`).
2. **`anchors queue`**: Lista as tarefas pendentes na fila.
3. **`anchors next`**: O agente de IA chama este comando para puxar o próximo card sem depender de prompting manual.
4. **`anchors work <alvo>`**: Emite o prompt contextual com as instruções exatas daquela etapa.
5. **`anchors deliver`**: O agente registra a entrega; o Anchors valida o resultado com gates.
6. **`anchors done <id>`**: Arquiva o card concluído no histórico.

---

## 2. Tratando Bloqueios e Escalonamento

- **`anchors escalate`**: Se a IA encontra uma ambiguidade na regra, ela estaciona o card em `needs-user` e abre uma issue.
- **`anchors unblock`**: Quando o desenvolvedor responde a dúvida, este comando destrava o card.
- **`anchors decided <card>`**: Retoma o fluxo com a decisão humana registrada.
